parts:
Hello All,

Is it possible to duplicate a `model` syntax into two or more models like `model1` and `model2` such that the ***free parameters*** in each duplicated model are suffixed/labeled differently?

Below is a toy example of what I hope to achieve:
```
model <- "y ~ x1 + x2
           ## Variances of x1 and x2 are 1
           x1 ~~ 1*x1
           x2 ~~ 1*x2
           ## x1 and x2 are correlated
           x1 ~~ x2"

#-DUPLICATE INTO TWO MODELS:

model1 <- "y ~ b1a*x1 + b2a*x2
           ## Variances of x1 and x2 are 1
           x1 ~~ 1*x1
           x2 ~~ 1*x2
           ## x1 and x2 are correlated
           x1 ~~ ra*x2"

model2 <- "y ~ b1b*x1 + b2b*x2
           ## Variances of x1 and x2 are 1
           x1 ~~ 1*x1
           x2 ~~ 1*x2
           ## x1 and x2 are correlated
           x1 ~~ rb*x2"
```
Much appreciated,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: lavaan syntax duplication
parts:
No sure if this is what you need. The model syntax is just a string. So you can add a placeholder (e.g., !!suffix!!) and the change it to anything you need using gsub()

``` r
model0 <- "
y ~ b1!!suffix!!*x1 + b2!!suffix!!*x2

## Variances of x1 and x2 are 1
x1 ~~ 1*x1
x2 ~~ 1*x2
## x1 and x2 are correlated

x1 ~~ r!!suffix!!*x2
"

modela <- gsub("!!suffix!!", "a", model0, fixed = TRUE)
modelb <- gsub("!!suffix!!", "b", model0, fixed = TRUE)

cat(modela)
#>
#> y ~ b1a*x1 + b2a*x2
#> ## Variances of x1 and x2 are 1
#> x1 ~~ 1*x1
#> x2 ~~ 1*x2
#> ## x1 and x2 are correlated
#> x1 ~~ ra*x2
cat(modelb)
#>
#> y ~ b1b*x1 + b2b*x2
#> ## Variances of x1 and x2 are 1
#> x1 ~~ 1*x1
#> x2 ~~ 1*x2
#> ## x1 and x2 are correlated
#> x1 ~~ rb*x2
```

<sup>Created on 2023-09-27 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

Hope this helps.

-- Shu Fai

parts:
I won't say it is impossible, but I think it is difficult, if you have to use a model syntax with no label as the input, and a model syntax as the output.

To know the free parameters present in a model syntax, you need to parse the model syntax. However, the model syntax parser in lavaan will parse the syntax to something else (e.g., a parameter table). As far as I know, this is a one-way trip. It won't tell you where in the model syntax the free parameters are, and so you can't use the parser to determine where to insert the labels.

Does the output have to be a model syntax? Can it be a parameter table? If yes, then it would be much easier to do so. Just generate the parameter table from the original model syntax without labels, and add the labels to the parameter table. The parameter table can then be used a model in sem(). (Care must be taken to ensure that the generated parameter table is as expected.)

-- Shu Fai

P.S.: Coincidentally, last week I wrote a function to convert a parameter table back to a model syntax (https://sfcheung.github.io/semhelpinghands/reference/ptable_to_syntax.html). However, it may not be what you need because it only generates a model syntax that is "functionally equivalent" to the one used to generate the parameter table. The generate syntax "looks" very different from the original model syntax.

I won't say it is impossible, but I think it is difficult, if you have to use a model syntax with no label as the input, and a model syntax as the output.

To know the free parameters present in a model syntax, you need to parse the model syntax. It won't tell you where in the model syntax the free parameters are, and so you can't use the parser to determine where to insert the labels.

Does the output have to be a model syntax? Can it be a parameter table? If yes, then it would be much easier to do so. Just generate the parameter table from the original model syntax without labels, and add the labels to the parameter table. The parameter table can then be used a model in sem(). (Care must be taken to ensure that the generated parameter table is as expected.)

Hi Simon,

admittedly very quick and dirty ... It's just to serve as an example ... You can add or change one or more labels via lavaanify this way:

library(lavaan)


label.param <- function(m, a) {
  if(class(m) != "data.frame") m <- lavaanify(m, model.type = "sem", auto = TRUE)
  m[m$lhs == a[[1]]["lhs"] & m$op == a[[1]]["op"] & m$rhs == a[[1]]["rhs"], "label"] <- a[[1]]["label"]
  if(length(a) > 1) {
    a[[1]] <- NULL
    label.param(m, a)
  }
  else {
    return(m)
  }
}


model <- "
ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3
dem60 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4
dem65 =~ y5 + y6 + y7 + y8
dem60 ~ ind60
dem65 ~ ind60 + dem60"


# Example 1
model1 <- label.param(
  model, list(
    c(lhs = "dem60", op = "~", rhs = "ind60", label = "xyz")
  )
)

fit1 <- sem(model1, PoliticalDemocracy)
parameterEstimates(fit1)


# Example 2
model2 <- label.param(
  model, list(
    c(lhs = "dem60", op = "~", rhs = "ind60", label = "a"),
    c(lhs = "dem65", op = "~", rhs = "dem60", label = "b"),
    c(lhs = "dem65", op = "~", rhs = "ind60", label = "c")
  )
)

fit2 <- sem(model2, PoliticalDemocracy)
parameterEstimates(fit2)



Does this help?

Thanks, Simon. Your question motivated me to think about working with the output of lavParseModelString(). I rarely use this function because it "just" parses the model string, as its name implies. Unlike lavaanify(), it does not create a complete parameter table, which includes parameters such as covariances and error variances that may not need to be specified in the model syntax because they are added automatically by lavaanify() .

Interestingly, in your case, the proper way to achieve what you want, which may also be what I or some others want to do sometimes, is to work on the output of lavParseModelString(), which I arbitrarily call an "incomplete parameter table." Exactly because it just parses the model string and add nothing else, it allows us to generate the original model syntax.

I revised ptable_to_syntax() (https://sfcheung.github.io/semhelpinghands/reference/ptable_to_syntax.html) to work with the output of  lavParseModelString(). However, due to the nature of the output of lavParseModelString(), I disabled this feature by default to prevent accidental usage. To allow  ptable_to_syntax() to work with the output of  lavParseModelString(), set allow_incomplete to TRUE. This feature is for advanced users who know what they are doing.

Please find an illustration at the end of this post. To label unlabelled free parameters, I drafted a simple function, label_free() (similar to Christian's label.param()).  This is the workflow:

- Use  lavParseModelString(),with as.data.frame. = TRUE, to generate an "incomplete parameter table."
- Label the free parameters. You can do it in your own way, or use label_free() .  It depends on the model you are going to work on.
- Use  ptable_to_syntax() to reproduce a model syntax string.

The layout of the reproduced model syntax certainly cannot be identical to the original model syntax. However, it should function in the same way, except for the labels.

Note that, unlike working with a proper parameter table, I do not yet know of a reliable way to compare the output of lavParseModelString(), and so I did not write a version of  compare_ptables() for the output of lavParseModelString(). Therefore, you need to check the output to make sure that the generated syntax is functionally identically to the original model syntax.

The revised function is in the latest version (0.1.9.9) of semhelpinghands at GitHub:

remotes::install_github("sfcheung/semhelpinghands")

Note that there is a lot of possibilities in specifying a model by syntax and I cannot guarantee that these functions will work for all cases (I already know cases in which they will not work and prevent them to work on those cases). Nevertheless, if you only need to do what you want to do in just a few possible models, then it is not difficult to check whether the results produced are what you need.

Personally, I still think it is more reliable to work on the model string itself and use function like gsub(). The process is more transparent and it is also easier check the results. This approach can also keep the layout and comments, which are lost when the string is parsed by lavParseModelString() . However, if the input model syntax must have its free parameters unlabelled, then I do not yet know of a solution that works directly on the model string. If there is one, I would like to know too.

Last, if you discovered any bugs, I would love to know. Thanks.

Hope this helps.

-- Shu Fai

``` r
library(lavaan)
#> This is lavaan 0.6-16
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.

library(semhelpinghands)
# Need at least Version 0.1.9.9 of semhelpinghands
# Can be installed from GitHub for now:
# remotes::install_github("sfcheung/semhelpinghands")

input <- "y ~ x1 + x2
          x1 ~~ 1*x1
          x2 ~~ 1*x2
          x1 ~~ x2"

# Create an "incomplete" data frame representation
input_df <- lavParseModelString(input, as.data.frame. = TRUE)

# Define a function to label unlabelled free parameters
label_free <- function(object,
                       pnames = NULL,
                       suffix = "") {
    i <- object$fixed == "" & object$label == ""
    q <- sum(i)
    if (q > 0) {
        if (is.null(pnames)) {
            pnames <- paste0("p", seq_len(q), suffix)
          } else {
            if (length(pnames) != q) {
                stop("The length of panmes ",
                     "does not match ",
                     "the number of unlabelled free parameters")
              }
            pnames <- paste0(pnames, suffix)
          }
        object[i, "label"] <- pnames
        return(object)
      } else {
        stop("No unlabelled free parameters.")
      }
  }

# Examples
# Use auto names for unlabelled parameters

tmp <- label_free(input_df,
                  suffix = "a")
tmp
#>   lhs op rhs mod.idx block fixed start lower upper label prior efa rv
#> 1   y  ~  x1       0     1                           p1a            
#> 2   y  ~  x2       0     1                           p2a            
#> 3  x1 ~~  x1       1     1     1                                    
#> 4  x2 ~~  x2       2     1     1                                    
#> 5  x1 ~~  x2       0     1                           p3a
output_a <- ptable_to_syntax(tmp,
                             allow_incomplete = TRUE)
cat(output_a, "\n")
#> y ~ p1a*x1 + p2a*x2

#> x1 ~~ 1*x1
#> x2 ~~ 1*x2

#> x1 ~~ p3a*x2

tmp <- label_free(input_df,
                  suffix = "b")
tmp
#>   lhs op rhs mod.idx block fixed start lower upper label prior efa rv
#> 1   y  ~  x1       0     1                           p1b            
#> 2   y  ~  x2       0     1                           p2b            
#> 3  x1 ~~  x1       1     1     1                                    
#> 4  x2 ~~  x2       2     1     1                                    
#> 5  x1 ~~  x2       0     1                           p3b
output_b <- ptable_to_syntax(tmp,
                             allow_incomplete = TRUE)
cat(output_b, "\n")
#> y ~ p1b*x1 + p2b*x2

#> x1 ~~ 1*x1
#> x2 ~~ 1*x2

#> x1 ~~ p3b*x2

# Examples
# Use user-supplied labels

tmp <- label_free(input_df,
                  pnames = c("b1", "b2", "r"),
                  suffix = "a")
tmp

#> 1   y  ~  x1       0     1                           b1a            
#> 2   y  ~  x2       0     1                           b2a            
#> 3  x1 ~~  x1       1     1     1                                    
#> 4  x2 ~~  x2       2     1     1                                    
#> 5  x1 ~~  x2       0     1                            ra
output_a <- ptable_to_syntax(tmp,
                             allow_incomplete = TRUE)
cat(output_a, "\n")
#> y ~ b1a*x1 + b2a*x2

#> x1 ~~ 1*x1
#> x2 ~~ 1*x2

#> x1 ~~ ra*x2

tmp <- label_free(input_df,
                  pnames = c("b1", "b2", "r"),
                  suffix = "b")
tmp
#>   lhs op rhs mod.idx block fixed start lower upper label prior efa rv
#> 1   y  ~  x1       0     1                           b1b            
#> 2   y  ~  x2       0     1                           b2b

Thanks, Simon. Your question motivated me to think about working with the output of lavParseModelString(). I rarely use this function because it "just" parses the model string, as its name implies. Unlike lavaanify(), it does not create a complete parameter table, which includes parameters such as covariances and error variances that may not need to be specified in the model syntax because they are added automatically by lavaanify() .

Interestingly, in your case, the proper way to achieve what you want, which may also be what I or some others want to do sometimes, is to work on the output of lavParseModelString(), which I arbitrarily call an "incomplete parameter table." Exactly because it just parses the model string and add nothing else, it allows us to generate the original model syntax.

I revised ptable_to_syntax() (https://sfcheung.github.io/semhelpinghands/reference/ptable_to_syntax.html) to work with the output of  lavParseModelString(). However, due to the nature of the output of lavParseModelString(), I disabled this feature by default to prevent accidental usage. To allow  ptable_to_syntax() to work with the output of  lavParseModelString(), set allow_incomplete to TRUE. This feature is for advanced users who know what they are doing.

Please find an illustration at the end of this post. To label unlabelled free parameters, I drafted a simple function, label_free() (similar to Christian's label.param()).  This is the workflow:

- Use  lavParseModelString(),with as.data.frame. = TRUE, to generate an "incomplete parameter table."
- Label the free parameters. You can do it in your own way, or use label_free() .  It depends on the model you are going to work on.
- Use  ptable_to_syntax() to reproduce a model syntax string.

The layout of the reproduced model syntax certainly cannot be identical to the original model syntax. However, it should function in the same way, except for the labels.

Note that, unlike working with a proper parameter table, I do not yet know of a reliable way to compare the output of lavParseModelString(), and so I did not write a version of  compare_ptables() for the output of lavParseModelString(). Therefore, you need to check the output to make sure that the generated syntax is functionally identically to the original model syntax.

The revised function is in the latest version (0.1.9.9) of semhelpinghands at GitHub:

remotes::install_github("sfcheung/semhelpinghands")

Note that there is a lot of possibilities in specifying a model by syntax and I cannot guarantee that these functions will work for all cases (I already know cases in which they will not work and prevent them to work on those cases). Nevertheless, if you only need to do what you want to do in just a few possible models, then it is not difficult to check whether the results produced are what you need.

Personally, I still think it is more reliable to work on the model string itself and use function like gsub(). The process is more transparent and it is also easier check the results. This approach can also keep the layout and comments, which are lost when the string is parsed by lavParseModelString() . However, if the input model syntax must have its free parameters unlabelled, then I do not yet know of a solution that works directly on the model string. If there is one, I would like to know too.

Last, if you discovered any bugs, I would love to know. Thanks.

Hope this helps.

-- Shu Fai

``` r

#> This is lavaan 0.6-16
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
library(semhelpinghands)
# Need at least Version 0.1.9.9 of semhelpinghands
# Can be installed from GitHub for now:
# remotes::install_github("sfcheung/semhelpinghands")

input <- "y ~ x1 + x2
          x1 ~~ 1*x1
          x2 ~~ 1*x2
          x1 ~~ x2"

# Create an "incomplete" data frame representation
input_df <- lavParseModelString(input, as.data.frame. = TRUE)

# Define a function to label unlabelled free parameters
label_free <- function(object,
                       pnames = NULL,
                       suffix = "") {
    i <- object$fixed == "" & object$label == ""
    q <- sum(i)
    if (q > 0) {
        if (is.null(pnames)) {
            pnames <- paste0("p", seq_len(q), suffix)
          } else {
            if (length(pnames) != q) {
                stop("The length of panmes ",
                     "does not match ",
                     "the number of unlabelled free parameters")
              }
            pnames <- paste0(pnames, suffix)
          }
        object[i, "label"] <- pnames
        return(object)
      } else {
        stop("No unlabelled free parameters.")
      }
  }

                  suffix = "a")
